scope: complete local text generation; quality gate separate
cache_condition: existing disk/JIT cache; not cold disk

devices.name: NPU Compute Accelerator Device
devices.reason: An MCDM device; WSL2's GPU-PV forwards WDDM display adapters only, so it has no device node here and nothing installed inside WSL reaches it. It does work from a Windows-side process -- onnxruntime>=1.25 plus the WindowsWorkload.EP.AMD.VitisAI.Framework appx, loading onnxruntime_vitisai_ep.dll (not the RyzenAI *Light* EP beside it) with its own directory on the DLL search path, against an A16W8-quantized opset-21 graph. Measured 5.3x the CPU on a 1024x2048x2048 GEMM. See vllm_omni/edge/npu_ryzenai.py.

devices.name: AMD Radeon(TM) 890M Graphics
devices.reason: No /dev/dri under WSL2, but reachable through DirectML over /dev/dxg: pip install torch-directml in its own venv (it pins torch==2.4.1). Measured 1.12 TFLOP/s fp32 and 5-7.4 GB/s -- below the CPU on both, so route work here only when the CPU is the thing you are trying to free.

devices.name: AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 w/ Radeon 890M
devices.reason: vllm.platforms.current_platform is 'cuda', not 'cpu': this interpreter's vLLM wheel has no CPU executor. The CPU build lives in a separate venv (.venvs/omni-cpu); a CPU plan from here is a plan for that interpreter, not something this one can run.

reservations.note: 5 safetensors shard(s), on-disk size
flat budget at 1x context; 248 MiB if the backend accounts 27 sliding layers separately
512-token prefill chunk x 12 live tensors
attention scratch, driver/allocator context
freed once the weights are resident; peaks with the largest shard
memory this engine does not own on a shared pool
fragmentation and allocator slack

kv_budget.summary: 720 MiB flat; 248 MiB if the backend accounts 27 sliding@512 layers separately (2.91x)

refusals.message: npu:amd executes exported graphs (['onnx:a16w8']), not checkpoints, so a whole autoregressive text session cannot be placed on it
refusals.remedy: place a single stage there instead, via vllm_omni.edge.local.external.stage.plan_external_stage; the decode loop stays on the CPU or the GPU because both of these devices read the same system memory it does

refusals.message: gpu_integrated:amd executes exported graphs (['onnx:fp16', 'onnx:fp32']), not checkpoints, so a whole autoregressive text session cannot be placed on it
refusals.remedy: place a single stage there instead, via vllm_omni.edge.local.external.stage.plan_external_stage; the decode loop stays on the CPU or the GPU because both of these devices read the same system memory it does

refusals.message: vllm.platforms.current_platform is 'cuda', not 'cpu': this interpreter's vLLM wheel has no CPU executor. The CPU build lives in a separate venv (.venvs/omni-cpu); a CPU plan from here is a plan for that interpreter, not something this one can run.
refusals.remedy: see the reason; masked devices are re-enabled by dropping them from --mask

fallbacks: shorter --max-model-len reduces the KV reservation linearly
notes: activations, workspace and the load transient are estimates (E); engine.py records the measured peak against them after the load

observed.per_process_gpu_attribution_reason: nvmlDeviceGetComputeRunningProcesses returned 0 process(es), none from this engine's tree of 3 PID(s): under WSL2 the GPU-PV driver reports no per-process compute list, so GPU bytes cannot be attributed to this engine's PIDs on this host. The load delta is a whole-card measurement.

cancel.note: a cancelled request's KV blocks return to vLLM's pool, which is pre-allocated; the device counter is therefore expected NOT to fall. What must fall is the in-flight count, and no retired-epoch event may be delivered.

reservations.note: 5 safetensors shard(s), on-disk size; the load moved +8.78 GiB on the device (whole-card delta), which bounds weights + backend context together and is not an attribution to the weights alone
flat budget at 1x context; 248 MiB if the backend accounts 27 sliding layers separately
512-token prefill chunk x 12 live tensors
attention scratch, driver/allocator context
freed once the weights are resident; peaks with the largest shard
memory this engine does not own on a shared pool
fragmentation and allocator slack

measured_peak.caveats: sampled every 0.25 s, so the peak is a lower bound; the counter is shared with other processes and the baseline subtraction only removes what was there before the load, not what arrived during it. A budget above the measured peak is the intended outcome -- this budget is a safe upper bound for admission, not a prediction.

peaks_during_load.note: peaks are lower bounds: anything shorter than interval_s is missed. nvml_device_used is the whole card including other processes; tree_pss includes a share of file-backed pages. These three counters are different accountings and must not be summed.
